More independence. More connection. More choice. More moments that matter.

Someone who believes extraordinary communities are built by empowering everyone within them, the people who call them home and the people who make them feel like home.

And someone with the commercial courage, operational capability and inspirational leadership to turn that vision into reality.

Because great customer experiences and strong commercial performance shouldn't be competing priorities. The best leaders know how to deliver both.

  • Drive a commercial turnaround. Take ownership of financial performance, workforce productivity and operational efficiency to build a sustainable, profitable future.
  • Reimagine residential living. Bring fresh thinking from hospitality, clinical care and customer experience to create environments where choice, independence and connection thrive.

  • Lead meaningful sustainable change. Improve operating models, bring people along on the journey and embed improvements that deliver lasting results.

You might be a clinician who knows there's a better way to deliver aged care.

You might be an experienced aged care executive ready to challenge traditional thinking.

Or you might come from hospitality, healthcare, retirement living or another complex, customer-focused industry.

We're less interested in where you've come from and more interested in what you can make possible.

  • You see compliance as the ultimate measure of success. Clinical excellence, safety and compliance are non-negotiable. But they're the foundation, not the ambition.

We're looking for someone who can balance the heart of a purpose-driven organisation with the commercial discipline of a successful business.

Why Kalyra?
Kalyra is a proudly South Australian organisation with a purpose that goes beyond providing care.

Their purpose is simple: "We exist so that people can live in communities where they feel they belong, enhancing living."
They're proud of their history, but equally excited about what's next.

This is your opportunity to challenge convention, inspire transformation and create communities where everyone, whether receiving services or providing them, feels empowered to thrive.
Could you be the executive who changes the way we think about ageing?

If you're an innovative, optimistic and commercially minded leader who believes residential aged care can be so much more, we'd love to hear from you.

Because at Kalyra, it's not just about adding years to life. It's about adding life to years.

At Harrison McMillan, our mission is simple: to change lives, one placement at a time. As a trusted recruitment partner to government and industry, we connect exceptional people with opportunities where they can make a genuine impact.

Harrison McMillan is seeking an experienced Lead Delivery Manager to join a major Federal Government agency. Working within the Infrastructure & Operational Support Branch, this pivotal role will oversee the delivery of Managed ICT services, acting as the primary conduit between external providers and internal technical teams.

The Opportunity

This is a high-level leadership role requiring an experienced professional to manage complex ICT service delivery, contractual obligations, and stakeholder relationships. You will be instrumental in the transition of new services, the management of SLAs, and the strategic planning of critical infrastructure projects, such as the upcoming Approach to Market for Windows 11 MOE and application packaging support.

You will work within a section responsible for the end-user desktop environment, including SOE, Active Directory, Exchange, and Microsoft endpoint management.

Key Responsibilities


  • Service Management: Oversee the successful delivery of Managed ICT services, ensuring alignment with contractual SLAs and KPIs.

  • Contract Lifecycle: Lead the review and renewal of managed service contracts.

  • Procurement & Planning: Identify technical risks and develop Statements of Requirements for complex Approaches to Market (ATM).

  • Transition Management: Lead the transition of new services or providers, ensuring service readiness and clear stakeholder expectations.

  • Stakeholder Engagement: Act as the primary liaison between vendors and internal teams; build and maintain strong relationships at both operational and executive levels.

  • Continuous Improvement: Facilitate service reviews, manage expectations, and maintain up-to-date documentation and escalation procedures.

  • Governance: Facilitate meetings, manage risks and issues, track action items, and ensure senior stakeholders remain informed and engaged.

Essential Experience & Skills


  • Delivery Expertise: Extensive experience managing technical projects and ICT service delivery.

  • Government Procurement: Demonstrated experience with the Approach to Market and tender processes within the Australian Public Service.

  • Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders.

  • Relationship Management: Proven ability to build strong, collaborative relationships across internal teams, customers, and external vendors.

  • Technical Proficiency: Strong understanding of IT Service Management (ITSM) principles (Incident, Problem, Change, and Request Management).

  • Strategic Capability: Alignment with SFIA Level 6 (Technology Service Management - ITMG).

  • Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to work effectively both independently and within high-paced, collaborative team environments.

Desirable Skills


  • 5+ years of experience in delivery management or service delivery.

  • Strong understanding of Agile methodologies and project management tools.

Security Clearance

Applicants must hold an active Negative Vetting Level 2 (NV2) security clearance.

Contract Details


  • Location: Canberra, ACT (Full-time onsite, 5 days per week)

  • Classification: EL2 Equivalent

  • Initial Contract: 12 months

  • Extension Options: 2 x 12-month extensions

  • Estimated Start Date: August 2026

  • Hours: Up to 40 hours per week

Why Apply?

This is a key leadership role within a critical government environment. You will have the opportunity to drive the operational efficiency of enterprise-level ICT services, influence procurement strategy, and work within a team responsible for the foundational infrastructure of government operations.

Note: Please be advised that the agency implements a contractor stand-down period during December and January (typically 4–6 weeks, at the department’s discretion).

Apply now or contact the Harrison McMillan team for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
Harrison McMillan has the privilege of partnering with Hepatitis SA to appoint their next Chief Executive Officer.

About Hepatitis SA
Hepatitis SA is the lead community-based, not-for-profit organisation responding to viral hepatitis, primarily hepatitis B and hepatitis C, in South Australia.

The organisation provides education, peer education, information, referral and support services for people affected by viral hepatitis, people at risk, health and welfare professionals, and the broader community. Hepatitis SA is also a Needle and Syringe Program secondary site and operates harm reduction peer services across various NSP sites in metropolitan Adelaide.

With a committed team, strong sector relationships and a community-led approach, Hepatitis SA plays an important role in public health, harm reduction, advocacy and providing services for priority populations.

About the role
Reporting to the Board, the CEO will lead the day-to-day management and implementation of the strategic direction of Hepatitis SA.

This is a broad, hands-on role spanning service delivery, advocacy, funding and financial management, people management and stakeholder engagement, and advising the Board on policy, strategic and operational direction, organisational risk and finances.

The incoming CEO will build on strong organisational foundations while strengthening funding sustainability, systems and processes and impact reporting

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead Hepatitis SA’s operations, programs and people
  • Ensure services remain responsive to communities affected by viral hepatitis
  • Oversee education, peer education, support and harm reduction programs
  • Manage budgets, grants, funding submissions, acquittals, tenders and reporting
  • Build strong relationships with funders, government, sector partners and community stakeholders
  • Represent Hepatitis SA in local, state and national forums
  • Advise the Board re strategy, governance, risk, and budget planning and monitoring
  • Lead and support a small, diverse team, including peer workers
  • Strengthen systems, policies, documentation and organisational processes
  • Communicate the impact of Hepatitis SA’s work to funders, partners and the broader community


What we’re looking for:

  • Experience: Senior leadership experience in health, human services, community, not-for-profit or related settings
  • Financial Capability: Strong skills in budgeting, grants, acquittals, funding reports and tenders
  • Governance Knowledge: Experience working effectively with a Board
  • Community Understanding: Appreciation of health promotion, harm reduction lived experience and peer-led programs
  • Ability to Navigate Complexity: Comfortable operating in challenging environments with the ability to work autonomously, exercise sound judgement, and navigate complexity with confidence.
  • Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Leadership Style: Practical, inclusive, non-judgemental and able to build trust with diverse communities
  • Flexibility: Ability to work flexibly and undertake some intrastate and interstate travel


Benefits:

  • Meaningful Impact: Lead work that directly supports people affected by viral hepatitis
  • Strong Foundations: Join a respected organisation with experienced staff and sector relationships
  • Sector Influence: Represent Hepatitis SA across local, state and national forums
  • Purpose-Led Work: Contribute to hepatitis B and C elimination goals, with a focus on equity and no-one left behind
  • Salary Packaging: Salary packaging arrangements are available
  • Flexible Working: WFH options may apply after the first 12 months, subject to performance and policy


Why join Hepatitis SA?
This is an opportunity to lead a respected, community-based organisation with deep community connections and an important role in South Australia’s public health landscape.

The coming years will be important for Hepatitis SA, with new National Strategies, a changing funding environment, ongoing advocacy and continued work toward the elimination of hepatitis B and hepatitis C as public health threats.

This role will suit a leader who is both strategic and practical; someone who can build on what is already working well while strengthening and evolving the organisation for the future.

If you are ready to bring your leadership, community focus and strategic capability to Hepatitis SA, please visit harrisonmcmillan.com.au or click APPLY NOW. We request applications include a CV and Cover Letter outlining your interest and suitability for the role. A position description is available upon request. Please note that the successful applicant will be required to undertake a police check.

For confidential enquiries, please contact Tamara Chambers – Client Delivery Lead on 0468039108

Harrison McMillan and Hepatitis SA are committed to an inclusive recruitment process. Applications are encouraged from people with diverse backgrounds and lived experiences, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, people with lived experience, and people from communities affected by viral hepatitis.

job.title: Technical Change Analyst (6753)
job.description:
At Harrison McMillan, our mission is simple: to change lives, one placement at a time

As a trusted recruitment partner to government and industry, we pride ourselves on connecting exceptional people with roles where they can truly make an impact

Harrison McMillan is seeking a Technical Change Analyst (APS6 equivalent) to work with a Federal Government Department in Canberra

Job details

The Technical Change Analyst will be an expert in preparing and implementing change and training artefacts to support stakeholders and end users to transition from current state to future state for ICT delivery projects

Deliverables


  • Discovery pack including identification of problem statement and vision, stakeholder map, personas and persona journeys, pain points and benefits (in collaboration with Business Analysts).

  • Change Management and Communications Planning support for both Business and End users.

  • Contributing to communication content, including emails, intranet posts, FAQs, briefing packs, and stakeholder updates

  • Contributing to the benefits realisation plan and provision of benefits realisation support, including collecting and validating baseline data, metrics, and success indicators.

  • Training Planning and Materials Development. Development of training content such as user guides, short format videos, and online learning modules.

Essential criteria


  • 3+ years previous experience in an ICT Change Analyst role delivering desired business outcomes in complex ICT projects

  • Knowledge of change management methodologies, tools and structure, and applying to ICT Delivery in a “Wagile” project utilising Agile rituals within Prince2 governance framework

  • Experience in assessing training needs and preparing training user guides, videos and online courses

  • Ability to prepare communication plans and deliver drafted and timely communications content as per business requirements

  • Experience with identifying benefits, supporting the delivery of benefits, and providing evidence-based outcomes of benefits realisation

  • Exceptional level of interpersonal, negotiation and communication skills and an ability to effectively develop strong working relationships with key internal and external stakeholders and operational staff

  • Persuasive oral and written communication skills including effectiveness in negotiation and liaison.

Desirable


  • Managing User Acceptance Testing with business and end users

  • Human centred design and designing with accessibility built in

  • Conducting user research to inform requirements and design

  • Working on secure government systems and in a complex global ICT environment

  • Project management systems, tools, and processes and how these are practically used in Agile and Waterfall environments (DevOps, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Project)

This role is a 12-month contract and requires a NV1 clearance
